label: III.69 n. 14 [26192] — Created things have proper actions through their likeness to the creator
interpretation: Aquinas argues against denying natural things operations of their own. Actual doing follows on actual being, with God as pure act and first cause as his example. The anti-occasionalist conclusion concerns created things receiving genuine activity. The chapter’s use of particular natural effects is part of the case for their genuine agency.
attribution: The passage states that in producing created things in being, God also communicates a likeness in acting, so that created things have actions of their own, which is the premise.
